app_documentation:
The Flower Delivery App is a modern e-commerce platform designed to streamline the process of browsing, purchasing, and tracking flower deliveries. Built with React for the frontend and Node.js/Express for the backend, the application provides an elegant, botanical-themed interface that prioritizes visual product discovery through high-quality imagery and intuitive navigation. The platform serves three primary user roles: Customers who browse and purchase flowers, Admins who manage inventory and pricing, and Delivery Drivers who fulfill orders.

The application's core features include a comprehensive flower catalog with category-based browsing, detailed product views with pricing and availability information, shopping cart management with real-time total calculations, and a streamlined checkout process integrated with Stripe for secure payment processing. Customers can track their orders in real-time with status updates and delivery notifications via email or SMS. The admin interface enables inventory management, allowing administrators to add new flowers, update stock levels, and manage product availability. All data is stored in a PostgreSQL database with tables for users, flowers, orders, order items, and cart items, ensuring robust data integrity and scalability.

Designed with a mobile-first approach, the app features a clean color scheme with rose pink (#E91E63) as the primary accent color, creating an inviting and premium feel. The interface uses bottom navigation for easy thumb access, touch-optimized components with minimum 44x44px targets for accessibility, and responsive layouts that adapt seamlessly across devices from 375px to 428px width. The application leverages AWS S3 for flower image storage, ensuring fast loading times and scalable media management. With WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, the platform ensures accessibility for all users through proper contrast ratios, screen reader support, and keyboard navigation capabilities.

Intended for both individual customers seeking convenient flower delivery services and businesses managing floral inventory, the Flower Delivery App combines elegant design with powerful functionality to create a seamless end-to-end experience from product discovery to doorstep delivery. The platform's architecture supports future scalability with bigint primary keys, indexed columns for performance optimization, and a modular design that allows for easy feature expansion and maintenance.

glossary.Catalog: The main browsing interface where customers view available flowers organized by categories such as Roses, Tulips, Lilies, Orchids, and Bouquets. The catalog displays product cards with images, names, prices, and stock availability.
glossary.Cart Items: Temporary shopping selections stored in the database that persist across user sessions. Cart items track the flower products, quantities, and timestamps of when items were added before checkout is completed.
glossary.Order Status: The current stage of an order in the fulfillment process, including states such as Pending (newly created), Processing (being prepared), Out for Delivery (assigned to driver), Delivered (completed), or Cancelled (terminated). Status changes trigger automated notifications to customers.
glossary.Stripe Integration: Third-party payment processing service integrated into the checkout flow to securely handle credit card transactions, tokenization, and payment confirmations. Ensures PCI compliance without storing sensitive payment data in the application database.
glossary.Stock Quantity: The available inventory count for each flower product maintained in the flowers table. Stock is decremented when orders are confirmed (not when added to cart) to prevent overselling, and admins can update quantities through the inventory management interface.
glossary.Baseline Artifact: A versioned snapshot of project documentation including requirements, design specifications, database schemas, and development plans that serves as a reference point for tracking changes, managing scope, and ensuring alignment across development cycles.
